checks.detail: sum(rays.i) = 10935.582569875034 for all three cases, bit-identical. A BSDF redirects rays in Optiland's model; it neither creates nor destroys energy, so any downstream throughput estimate must come from the spatial distribution, not from the total.

checks.detail: RMS radius 0.1580 mm unscattered -> 0.8829 mm with sigma=0.01, against the 0.5244 mm predicted by combining the unscattered spot with sigma*L = 0.5000 mm in quadrature (ratio 1.684). checks.detail: two runs with np.random.seed(7) set immediately before each trace give RMS radii 0.879901 and 0.894819 mm (1.67% apart). optiland.scatter is numba-compiled and its RNG is not reachable from numpy, so a scattering result CANNOT be frozen as a bit-exact repository fixture.
checks.name: numpy_seeding_does_not_make_bsdf_scattering_reproducible
